$comment: One flat register under `### Medium/Low-Priority Risks`, which is the literal heading
test-design-qa-template.md ships, over a table carrying both a Risk ID and a Score column. Every risk
is correct: right category, right scale, right arithmetic, right coverage, right priority order.
It is here because the band check used to count only the rows that sat under a heading declaring a
range. One rangeless heading therefore took the denominator to zero and a score-9 risk filed beneath
it scored a clean 100%, which is the flagship defect this suite exists to catch passing as a
well-formed document. The check now holds every row, so this case fails five times over.
The document is CONSTRUCTED: seeded-correct-run's five risks, merged into one table under the
rangeless heading, with nothing else changed.
derivation: Five rows, all well formed, all in scale, all arithmetically correct, so wellFormedIds,
validCategories, inScale and arithmeticOk are 5 each.
Bands: neither `### Medium/Low-Priority Risks` nor its parent `## Risk Assessment` declares a range,
so no enclosing heading places any row. banded is 5 because every row is held to the check, and
bandOk is 0. Each of the five failures records a null heading and the reason that no enclosing
Everything else is seeded-correct-run's. Grounding is 5 of 5 with no top-severity miss, risk links
resolve 5 of 5, coverage satisfies 5 of 5, and all nine ordering pairs resolve and pass. That is the
point of the case: one structural omission, and nothing else wrong.
`ordering` carries `flattened`, which is true when every material risk that reached a priority reached
the same one. A plan like that satisfies every pairwise constraint without ordering anything, so the
metric reports unmeasurable rather than a perfect score.
`unscoredRiskTables` records every table that names risks with an `R-NNN` id and states no score. Such a
table cannot be scored and used to be skipped without a word, so a register split across a scored table
and an unscored one lost its second half silently. The threshold on the count is zero.
